title: Postscript: A Brief History of Why the U.S. Consumer Thinks the Way They Do
supportedClaims: Modern American money behavior was shaped by a specific postwar history, not by timeless human nature.
Low rates, housing shortage, demobilization, and policy choices after 1945 encouraged borrowing, homebuilding, and consumer demand until those habits felt normal and morally neutral.
The practical lesson is to treat present defaults around credit, housing, and consumer optimism as historical inheritances that deserve examination rather than automatic obedience.
caution: A historical explanation is not a blanket indictment of consumption. It is a reminder that social defaults are contingent and can stop fitting new conditions.
